labels.rationale: The prompt explicitly says a presentation is one diagram that evolves through steps instead of a deck of separate slides.

labels.intent: Each step is individually identifiable and defines the diagram state shown while it is active.
labels.rationale: Per-step diagram state follows directly from the prompt; a stable id and especially a section/era label are the reference's structural choices.

labels.intent: Each step carries its own narration text, presented in a way suited to both presenting and browsing.
labels.rationale: The prompt requires a caption per step and two viewing modes; splitting narration into a one-line title plus a paragraph caption is one reasonable form.

labels.intent: Step numbers shown to viewers stay correct when steps are inserted, removed, or reordered, without manual bookkeeping.
labels.rationale: Correct step numbering is a basic of navigable steps; deriving numbers from order is one way to guarantee it.
Type-cast-free generics at the component boundary are a developer-ergonomics choice the prompt does not imply.
The prompt says elements move and get relabeled as the diagram evolves, which requires persisting entities to change in place rather than being redrawn.

labels.intent: Elements introduced by a step visibly animate in, coordinated with persisting elements' movement so the transition reads clearly.
labels.rationale: The prompt requires elements to appear; sequencing entrances strictly after persisting entities settle is one choreography choice.
An animated evolving diagram obviously needs removed elements to leave via a transition rather than vanishing abruptly; it is the counterpart of elements appearing.

labels.intent: Successive states of the same diagram keep scene continuity so entities morph rather than the scene being torn down and rebuilt between steps.
labels.rationale: Continuity is required by the evolving-diagram premise; a shared scene group that avoids remounting is one mechanism.

labels.intent: Entities that continue between steps are animated as morphs of the same element, never treated as new arrivals that fade in again.
labels.rationale: Treating continuing entities as continuous is required by the evolving model; layout projection is the reference's specific technique.
Preserving deliberately overlapping compositions under a specific implementation pattern is a refinement the prompt does not imply; its absence would rarely be noticed as incomplete.
The prompt does not ask for a style-free kit; shipping reusable components with a default theme would still satisfy it.

labels.intent: Individual presentations can customize the visual appearance of kit-rendered elements and chrome.
labels.rationale: Reusable components serving many topics plausibly need per-presentation customization, but stable DOM class/data hooks are one mechanism.
Whether the kit depends on a styling framework is an incidental technology choice not implied by the prompt.

labels.intent: Authors can position elements precisely per step and can go beyond the provided primitives when they do not fit a diagram's shape.
labels.rationale: Diagrams whose elements move need positional control; the specific escape hatch (raw motion elements with layoutIds) is one choice.
An attribution link is not asked for or implied by the prompt.
Verbatim attribution wording is an incidental value not implied by the prompt.
A styling hook for an attribution link only matters if the unrequested attribution exists.
Whether a brand link appears top-left is incidental branding not implied by the prompt.
The prompt explicitly requires viewers to switch between presenting and browsing.
Letting a presentation declare its opening mode is a convenience the prompt does not imply.

labels.intent: Present mode is optimized for live delivery, foregrounding the diagram with minimal text and chrome, and is distinct from browse mode.
labels.rationale: The prompt requires a presenting mode; exactly which elements are shown or hidden is the reference's choice.

labels.intent: Browse mode supports self-guided reading: it shows each step's full caption plus on-screen controls to move between steps and see progress.
labels.rationale: The prompt requires a browsing mode and per-step captions; the exact set of chrome (TOC on wide viewports, progress indicators) is the reference's choice.
Switching between presenting and browsing obviously should not lose the viewer's place; resetting the step would be a defect.

labels.intent: Viewers can advance and go back one step from the keyboard using conventional presentation keys.
labels.rationale: Keyboard step navigation is an obviously implied basic of moving through steps; the exact key set beyond common conventions is incidental.

labels.intent: Viewers on touch devices can move between steps in every mode, including when on-screen controls are hidden.
labels.rationale: The prompt's multi-screen-size requirement implies touch use; horizontal swipe is one mechanism.

labels.intent: Viewers can jump directly to an arbitrary step without stepping through the intermediate ones.
labels.rationale: Browsing implies non-linear access; activating a progress indicator is one mechanism.
A section/era-organized table of contents is the reference's structural choice; direct jumping is already covered elsewhere.

labels.intent: Navigation UI identifies the current step both visually and to assistive technology, and that state can be styled per presentation.
labels.rationale: Indicating the current step is a basic of step navigation; the specific semantic attribute and hook are reference choices.
A keyboard navigation handler that hijacks keys from focused controls (e.g., Space on a button double-advancing) is a robustness defect in the navigation the prompt asks for.

labels.intent: Navigating past the first or last step behaves predictably and never goes out of range or errors.
labels.rationale: Boundary handling is required for correctness; clamping with no wrap-around is one reasonable policy.

labels.intent: The diagram stays correctly composed and legible across viewport sizes, without its internal layout breaking, and morphs remain clean.
labels.rationale: The prompt requires the presentation to look right at different screen sizes; a fixed canvas scaled uniformly is one mechanism.
Specific canvas dimensions are an incidental value not implied by the prompt.

labels.intent: The diagram fits correctly in both the present and browse layouts despite their different surrounding chrome.
labels.rationale: Looking right in both modes is required; separate per-mode fit geometry is one way to achieve it.
The prompt says the skill turns a topic into a presentation and does not ask for interactive questioning, let alone one question at a time.

labels.intent: The skill establishes the topic, the visual style, and the content of each step, whether from the user or by deriving them.
labels.rationale: Producing a presentation requires deciding these things; gathering all of them from the user is one approach given a topic-only prompt.
The prompt frames the skill as turning a topic into a presentation, so asking rather than inferring missing details is a design preference, not a requirement.

labels.intent: The skill can produce a presentation without requiring the user to specify every detail up front, and supports iterating afterward.
labels.rationale: Turning just a topic into a presentation implies generating from partial input; the no-hard-gate wording is the reference's framing.
Permission to skip questions when the prompt is complete is an optional behavior with no completeness consequence.
ASCII mockups are an optional interaction technique the prompt does not imply.
The prompt explicitly requires the skill to work in projects that lack the scene components, which means detecting and scaffolding missing infrastructure.

labels.intent: Bootstrapping ensures a working build setup with a build command capable of building and serving the presentations.
labels.rationale: A working build is required to build and render; the specific Vite + React + TypeScript stack is a reasonable choice matching the starter repo, not the only one.
The prompt requires reusable scene components; an engine providing the step contract, morphing stage, present/browse navigation, captions, and fit-to-screen canvas is what those prompt features need.

labels.intent: Multiple presentations (including the sample) can coexist in one project, each individually reachable.
labels.rationale: A repo with a sample plus generated presentations needs coexistence; a route-mapping registry is one mechanism.

labels.intent: Detection of existing infrastructure is robust to cosmetic differences, so working setups are not needlessly re-scaffolded or overwritten.
labels.rationale: Robust detection follows from working in varied projects; keying on contract-level anchors is the reference's specific approach.

labels.intent: When scaffolding, the skill installs every dependency the generated presentation and its verification need, without assuming any are present.
labels.rationale: Working in an unscaffolded project requires installing dependencies; the specific package list is the reference's.
Whether the scaffold ships with a styling framework or default theme is a taste choice not implied by the prompt.

labels.intent: The skill reliably locates or obtains its bootstrap resources regardless of the user's current working directory.
labels.rationale: Resource lookup must not break depending on cwd; resolving relative to the SKILL.md directory is one mechanism.
The prompt explicitly requires the skill to work in a project without the scene components set up.
Re-scaffolding an already-set-up project would be wasteful or destructive; skipping is the obvious correct behavior.
Working in partially set-up projects without clobbering what exists is an obvious robustness requirement of self-bootstrapping.
Monorepo handling and the specific presentations/ location are not implied by the prompt.
Where the app is scaffolded in a standalone project is an incidental placement choice.

labels.intent: Before adding scaffolding to an existing non-empty project, the skill makes the target location clear and avoids unwanted or destructive writes.
labels.rationale: Safely writing into an existing project is a robustness basic; stating the target and requiring confirmation is one mechanism.

labels.intent: Each new presentation is separately reachable and added without interfering with other presentations.
labels.rationale: Coexistence and reachability are needed; a self-contained folder plus registry entry is the reference's structure.
Where styling lives (presentation vs kit) is an architecture/taste choice following the unrequested style-free kit decision.
Plain CSS as the default styling approach is a taste choice.
Generating a new presentation must not break existing ones such as the committed sample; this is basic correctness.
The prompt asks for a skill that turns a topic into a presentation; modifying existing presentations is reasonable but not requested or clearly implied.
Depends on the unrequested modify flow; not graded if modification is out of the prompt's scope.
Depends on the unrequested modify flow; scoping of edits is not implied by the prompt.
The prompt explicitly requires the skill to check that what it generates builds and renders; browser verification before reporting done is that requirement.

labels.intent: The skill's visual check covers representative steps (including dense or key ones and the ends) and the viewport sizes the presentation must support.
labels.rationale: Looking right at different screen sizes implies checking more than one view; the exact first/last/dense/narrow set is the reference's choice.
A check that does not lead to fixing failures, or that allows reporting success while failing, defeats the prompt's build-and-render check.
Where screenshot helper scripts live is an incidental tooling choice.
Building cleanly is directly required by the prompt's 'actually builds' check.
Rendering without errors is directly required by the prompt's 'renders' check.
The prompt requires each step to have its own caption and viewers to move through the steps.
The prompt defines presentations as one evolving diagram rather than slides; generated output must follow that.
Content fitting, readable overlaps, and no collisions with chrome are the general meaning of the prompt's 'look right', which the skill's visual check must confirm.

labels.intent: When automated checks flag possible visual problems, the skill investigates them, fixes genuine problems, and only accepts flagged items that are intentional and acceptable.
labels.rationale: Acting on findings is required if such tooling exists, but the warning-emitting helper itself is a reference mechanism.

labels.intent: Generated presentations make the current step visibly distinct in their navigation chrome.
labels.rationale: Seeing where you are is a navigation basic; attribution legibility and kit style-neutrality are unrequested reference choices.
The prompt asks for a way to verify presentations automatically; a full build that fails on errors is the core of that.

labels.rationale: The prompt fixes the sample's subject; the exact title and closing self-reference reveal are the reference's content choices.

labels.intent: The sample is one continuously evolving scene that builds on what is already on screen rather than switching to unrelated compositions.
labels.rationale: The evolving-scene behavior is required; the specific conversation row, card tray, and reveal frame layout are content choices.
The exact step count and era grouping of the sample are incidental content choices.

labels.intent: Verification confirms the committed sample presentation is present, reachable, and contains its expected steps.
labels.rationale: Verifying the sample is reasonable for the requested automatic verification, but checking nine canonical titles and captions is tied to reference-specific content.

labels.intent: Verification does not silently pass when a presentation it is meant to check is missing.
labels.rationale: A verifier that passes on absent input is a correctness defect; failing specifically on the reference sample is the reference's framing.

labels.intent: Automated verification renders every step of the checked presentation(s) in an environment faithful to real viewing and fails on runtime or console errors.
labels.rationale: Rendering every step is the natural meaning of automatically verifying presentations render; a real browser over a production preview is the reference's mechanism.
Using a specific loopback address is an environment-specific implementation detail; its absence only matters if localhost resolution breaks in a given environment.
Automated render verification must fail on browser errors, and identifying the failing step is a basic of actionable error reporting.
Verifying 'automatically' requires an unambiguous pass/fail result with a non-zero exit on failure.
An automated verifier that leaves preview servers running, especially after failures, is a robustness defect.

labels.intent: Visual review is supported by a repeatable way to capture views of each step of a presentation.
labels.rationale: The skill's visual check needs some capture mechanism, but a scaffolded project-local screenshot helper with a fixed artifact directory is one choice.

labels.intent: Visual captures reflect each step's settled state, not mid-transition frames.
labels.rationale: Capturing mid-animation would make visual review wrong; a configured settle interval is one mechanism.
Automated overlap heuristics are an extra the prompt does not imply.
An allow-overlap marker only matters for the unrequested overlap-warning heuristic.
Automated active-chrome distinctness warnings are an extra the prompt does not imply.
Attribution polish warnings depend on the unrequested attribution link.
Whether screenshot artifacts are advisory is an incidental tooling decision.

labels.intent: Automatic verification is available from a single, documented entry point that runs the build and the render checks.
labels.rationale: A clear entry point is needed for automatic verification; the specific npm script name is incidental.

labels.intent: The render check runs in an environment that faithfully executes the presentation, including layout and animation, rather than a superficial component mount.
labels.rationale: Faithful render checking is needed; Playwright, Chromium, and vite preview are one toolchain.

labels.intent: External tooling can enumerate the steps and observe the current step without depending on fragile DOM structure.
labels.rationale: Automated verification needs to step through all steps; data-step-count/data-step-index attributes are one mechanism.
A landing page and the per-slug URL scheme are incidental routing choices; reachability is covered elsewhere.
Explicit registry versus auto-discovery is an implementation preference with no prompt-implied consequence.
Avoiding a routing-library dependency is an incidental technology choice.

labels.intent: The reusable components are topic-agnostic building blocks that presentations on any topic can compose.
labels.rationale: Reusable scene components imply topic-agnostic parts; the specific primitive set is the reference's.
The icon library is an incidental technology choice.

labels.intent: The components the skill bootstraps into new projects match the repository's reusable components and cannot silently diverge from them.
labels.rationale: Bootstrapping must deliver the same reusable components; a template snapshot with parity checks is one mechanism.
A specific mode-toggle key binding is beyond common conventions and not implied by the prompt.
The sample's opening mode is an incidental choice.
